property_summary: For any depositor and any admissible amount, a (possibly re-entrant) withdrawal must not transfer more than that depositor's credit because credit is cleared before the external call; the mutant leaves credit set during the external call, so a re-entrant re-withdrawal underflows balance and reverts, which the re-entrant attacker surfaces as a failed outer call.

After a reentrant attacker fully drains its credit via withdrawAll, contract C's ether balance must be zero (each unit of credit can be withdrawn only once, since credit is zeroed before the external call); the mutant clears credit only after the call, so the reentrant second withdrawal pays out twice and leaves the invariant broken for some fuzzed amount.

A depositor can withdraw each unit of credit exactly once: if an attacker re-enters withdrawAll during its payout, total ether paid out must equal its deposit (reference zeroes credit before the external call); the mutant pays the credit twice during reentrancy, so the attacker receives more than it deposited.
For any depositor whose external call fails, withdrawAll must revert (the transfer failure aborts the withdrawal); the mutant deletes require(callResult) and thus completes without reverting.

property_summary: If withdrawAll completes without reverting, the caller must actually have received the withdrawn credit (call succeeded); C guarantees this via require(callResult), while M can 'succeed' while the external transfer failed, paying nothing.

If a caller's outgoing transfer fails, C preserves the caller's credit unchanged (the require reverts the state changes), whereas M zeroes the credit and balance even when the caller received nothing; the helper wallet's receive always reverts so the transfer fails for every fuzzed amount.

property_summary: Rule: whenever withdrawAll() completes without reverting, the contract's balance must actually decrease by the full withdrawn credit (the external transfer truly succeeded); the mutant drops require(callResult), so for a counterparty that reverts, withdrawAll 'succeeds' while c's balance is unchanged.

For any admissible input, if a caller with positive credit calls withdrawAll and it does not revert, then all of the contract's ether must actually have been paid out (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant drops require(callResult), so with a failing callee withdrawAll completes while c still holds the entire deposit.

For every deposit amount and actor, withdrawing all credited funds must pay out exactly the credited amount exactly once and leave the contract (and its internal balance ledger) consistent with its real ether holdings — the mutant skips decrementing the internal balance ledger during withdrawAll, so through a re-entrant counterparty the ledger diverges from address(c).balance and the payout/ledger conservation invariant breaks for some amount.
